text: Open-Meteo provides hourly PM2.5 and AQI forecast fields and can return missing values.
Open-Meteo documents air-quality forecasts up to seven forecast days, with five days as default.
Open-Meteo requires clear attribution to Open-Meteo and the CAMS ENSEMBLE data provider.
A certified respirator works best when it is well fitted and used correctly; children and elderly people need appropriate fit and comfort checks.
Keep windows closed during high outdoor particle periods, unless a verified indoor safety or ventilation need requires brief opening.
Choose an appropriately sized purifier and follow the manufacturer's clean-air capacity and maintenance instructions.
A homemade box-fan filter is supplemental, must use compatible parts, and should not be left unattended or used with damaged wiring.
Use chimney or exhaust ventilation while cooking and after completion, while checking outdoor air conditions.
A damp mop can reduce the re-suspension of settled dust compared with dry sweeping; avoid wetting electrical areas.
Avoid indoor incense, mosquito coil and biomass smoke when alternatives are available, especially around children and elderly members.
Walking or cycling avoids direct fuel use but may increase breathing exposure in heavy traffic, so use quieter lower-AQI routes.
Shared metro or bus travel can avoid a private-car journey, subject to local air quality inside the vehicle.
Induction avoids on-site biomass combustion but its emissions depend on the electricity source and may affect household costs.
LPG generally avoids solid-fuel smoke but still requires ventilation and safe appliance use.
Wood or coal heating can add indoor PM2.5. A safer indoor space should use ventilation and any cleaner available alternative.
Insulation and layering can reduce heating demand, but they do not replace safe ventilation or medical care.
Outdoor or delivery workers should take breaks, fit masks correctly and follow their employer's heat and safety procedures.
Children may breathe more relative to body size during activity; this app uses a planning multiplier, not a clinical rule.
Elderly people should receive a visible doctor and symptom reminder; this app is not a diagnostic service.
This app does not diagnose disease or prescribe medicine. Symptoms or difficult breathing should be discussed with a doctor or urgent service.
Seek urgent medical help for severe breathing difficulty, chest pain or confusion instead of relying on an air-quality estimate.
